newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ARIZONA CARDINALS DRAFT PICK CHARGED WITH SEXUAL ABUSE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ARIZONA CARDINALS DRAFT PICK CHARGED WITH SEXUAL ABUSE.

text.p: A top draft pick of the Arizona Cardinals National Football League team was charged on Wednesday with four felony counts of sexual abuse against women at a local night spot.
Jake "The Snake" Plummer, the Cardinals' second-round selection, also was charged with one count of misdemeanor assault in a criminal complaint released on Wednesday.
Plummer could face up to eight years and six months in prison if convicted of all the charges. An initial court appearance has been set for June 10.
The star quarterback led Arizona State University to the Rose Bowl game in January, although the team lost to Ohio State.
He allegedly engaged in sexual contact with four women at a local nightclub in March. The women claim Plummer groped them while on the dance floor without their consent and assaulted one of them.
Attorneys for three of the women recently announced they had reached a civil settlement with Plummer. Terms were not disclosed.
However, Rick Romley, Maricopa County Attorney, said the settlement did not affect his investigation.

"The payment of money cannot buy the silence of a victim or a witness to a criminal act," Romley said. "To permit such conduct would create two systems of justice -- one for the rich and one for the poor. This is not acceptable in Arizona."
Plummer could not immediately be reached for comment on Wednesday. He has declined to be interviewed by authorities throughout the course of the investigation.
The Cardinals released a statement, saying they had been advised of the charges and will monitor the situation.
"The Cardinals are anxious for Jake's side of the story to become public," team officials said in a brief statement.
A team spokesman said they expect the quarterback to be at the Cardinals' rookie and free agent mini-camp next month in Flagstaff, Arizona.
